quote: College teaches you subjects. It does not teach you to ship something another person depends on. That gap is the entire reason this community exists.
You do not need to arrive knowing anything. You need to be the kind of person who opens the thing up to see how it works — we can teach the rest in order.
Five tracks, taught in sequence, starting from the beginning. No jumping straight to the exciting part, because the exciting part only makes sense once the boring part is automatic.
We bring in people who do this for a living, so members hear how the field actually works rather than how a syllabus says it works.
Every member should finish their first season with a repository someone else could clone, read and run. That artefact is worth more than any certificate we could print.
Break it, understand it, defend it — in that order, inside a lab, with permission. The ethics are not a disclaimer bolted on at the end; they are the first thing we teach.
A photographer at every event, a writeup after every competition. Documentation is the difference between a club that happened and a club people remember.
The measure of this community is not what the current council builds. It is whether the people we hand it to make it better than we did.
